Journal of advanced research 2026-Oct-30 Medium

Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.

This review describes how single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, especially scATAC-seq, are being used to map the epigenetic regulatory programs that control bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It synthesizes recent findings into an atlas-level view of bone cell fate and function at single-cell resolution.

JMIR medical informatics 2026-Oct-29 Medium

A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.

This paper develops a knowledge graph that organizes Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with emotional comorbidities such as anxiety, depression, and insomnia, linking syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs to their sources. It then evaluates how well the graph supports generated answers using a blinded question-answering assessment. The work demonstrates a domain-specific approach to structuring TCM knowledge and testing its utility for retrieval-augmented answering.

Poultry science 2026-Oct-28 Medium

Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.

This study combined cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) with two ensemble machine learning methods, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine, to identify informative SNP markers associated with body weight in broiler chickens at hatch and 3 weeks of age. The approach demonstrates that affordable reduced-representation sequencing paired with ML can substitute for expensive high-density SNP arrays in genome-wide association studies for poultry breeding. The work offers a practical framework for resource-limited breeding programs seeking to identify trait-associated markers.

Plant biotechnology journal 2026-Oct-28 Medium

Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.

This paper describes how the CABBI center used a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to engineer C4 grasses (such as sugarcane, sorghum, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol oils in vegetative tissues for renewable fuels and biobased chemicals. It highlights the need to coordinate molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program, and shares lessons from applying this integrated approach across three C4 feedstocks.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-Oct-27 Medium

Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.

This paper computes phenologs—statistical overlaps between human disease genes and model-organism phenotype genes linked by orthology—at knowledge-graph scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph across human and seven model species. By leveraging PANTHER protein families, the authors produce a catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases, including cross-species mappings such as mouse-to-slime-mold, demonstrating that even distantly related organisms can inform human disease gene discovery.

OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.

OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, enabling auditable and reusable evidence for zoonotic emergence research.

Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.

This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict the onset of acute kidney injury and to forecast patient prognosis after AKI occurs. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data that challenge conventional machine learning methods, aiming to support earlier prevention and better post-onset care decisions.

Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.

This paper develops and evaluates a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate cross-domain knowledge for mental health, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to better capture the complexity, heterogeneity, and comorbidity of psychiatric disorders by combining dimensional models and domain-specific ontologies into a unified framework.

scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.

scSpatial is a new atlas/database that aggregates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance.

The authors present an evidence-aware AI framework that integrates heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data—FAERS adverse event reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records—using LLM-based information extraction combined with ontology-driven semantic integration. The work addresses the challenge of reconciling differences in data structure, terminology, evidence quality, and provenance across sources to build reliable knowledge resources for drug safety monitoring.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-Oct-21 Medium

The Drosophila Secretome.

This preprint describes a systematic computational assembly of the Drosophila secretome by analyzing all fly protein sequences with multiple tools and integrating FlyBase, UniProt, Gene Ontology, and large-scale proteomics data. The resulting resource catalogs secreted proteins in the fly, many of which are conserved in humans, providing a foundation for studying development, immunity, cancer, and neurobiology in a model organism.

Nutrients 2026-Oct-19 Low

Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.

This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary advice to individuals using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—has advanced rapidly in discovery but lags in clinical translation because evidence is fragmented across life stages and poorly integrated with systems biology. The authors call for lifespan-spanning frameworks that account for how nutritional needs and response heterogeneity change from preconception onward.

Cell reports methods 2026-Nov-12 High

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in the field: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and explicitly modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large transcriptomic atlases.

gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.

gcPathogen 2.0 is a major update to a pathogen genomic surveillance database, expanding coverage from 1,134 to 1,506 pathogenic species and surpassing 2.3 million genomic records. The update adds integrated genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale antimicrobial peptide discovery, supporting One Health research across bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites.

Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.

Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that supports standardized deposition of project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows. It houses over 7.7 million reference spectra and offers online analysis and disease-focused knowledge mining, addressing the growing need for metabolomics data storage and reuse.

Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.

ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized AI agents over heterogeneous biomedical data and networks. It aims to overcome the fragmentation of specialized tools by letting users interact in natural language while agents handle data integration and analysis. The work is a platform development study demonstrating a workflow-level approach to in silico repurposing.

Nucleic acids research 2026-Nov-02 Medium

InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.

InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, giving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and cross-links to resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. It remains a core reference resource for protein functional annotation.

Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.

The Journal of investigative dermatology 2026-Nov-01 Medium

Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.

This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes rapidly trigger extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 T cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had similar protein profiles regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps induced by the two strains showed distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in skin immunity.

CPT: pharmacometrics & systems pharmacology 2026-Nov-01 Medium

Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.

This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this view, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic modeling is used in drug development.

Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society 2026-Nov-01 Medium

PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.

PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to Protein Data Bank structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the previous internal PDBe pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast, scalable sequence search, a better bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on proprietary infrastructure.

EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.

EchoGO is a reproducible framework for functional enrichment of transcriptomic data that runs GOseq enrichment while comparing results across multiple organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. It assembles evidence at the GO-term level with provenance information, helping researchers address incomplete annotation and identifier-recognition issues. The tool is aimed at improving the interpretability of downstream functional analysis.

Frontiers in neuroergonomics 2026--01 Low

Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states.

This hypothesis paper proposes a framework for 'closed-loop cognitive state control,' treating cognition as a partially observable dynamical system whose latent states are inferred from multimodal behavioral, physiological, and contextual signals. The goal is to enable rapid entry into, stabilization of, and recovery of an individual's highest task-specific cognitive state through real-time estimation and intervention. It is a conceptual proposal rather than an empirical study, outlining a neuroengineering objective rather than reporting validated results.

Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

This review argues that AI-generated predictions of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities are often treated as equivalent to experimentally confirmed ones, which is a key reason most attempts to exploit metabolic plasticity therapeutically fail. It frames the distinction between computational hypotheses and experimental evidence as the starting point for evaluating AI and genome-scale systems biology approaches to identifying synthetic lethal targets.

Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.

This review argues that AI can be applied as a structured toolkit across the antibacterial drug discovery pipeline to counter antimicrobial resistance, rather than as an undefined add-on. It maps AI strengths—multi-omics integration, pattern recognition, and complex modeling—onto specific resistance mechanisms and translational stages, from target identification to clinical development. The paper aims to clarify where and how AI methods should be deployed to address slow antibiotic discovery and limited target diversity.

Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health.

This perspective proposes "sustainable nutrition" as a unifying concept that links dietary intake and health outcomes with food production, processing, access, and environmental sustainability. It argues that advancing public and planetary health requires understanding nutrition within these broader food-system contexts rather than focusing on intake and metabolism alone. The paper is conceptual and agenda-setting rather than presenting new data.
